html:
In the Estonian War of Independence, from 1918 to 1920, the new Republic of Estonia fought off the Soviet Red Army and then German forces, and won recognition from Soviet Russia.

Estonia had declared independence on 24 February 1918, a day before German troops occupied it. When the Germans left that November, the Red Army invaded and came within a few dozen kilometres of Tallinn. With British naval help and Finnish volunteers, Estonian forces drove it back and in 1919 also beat the Baltic German Landeswehr in Latvia.

By the Treaty of Tartu of 2 February 1920 Soviet Russia recognised Estonia forever. Independence lasted until the Soviet occupation of 1940 and the deportations that followed. The neighbouring Latvian war ran at the same time.
sum: In the Estonian War of Independence, from 1918 to 1920, the new Republic of Estonia fought off the Soviet Red Army and then German forces, and won recognition from Soviet Russia.
